name: SLS Buenos Aires Puerto Madero
positioning: Contemporary all-suite SLS hotel in Puerto Madero, Buenos Aires, with interiors by Piero Lissoni; the brand's first hotel in South America
best_for: Travelers who want contemporary design and a balcony over the city or the docks
Guests who want a spa, outdoor pool and an Argentinean grill with Japanese influences under one roof

facts.text: SLS Puerto Madero is SLS's first hotel in South America.
The hotel is at Juana Manso 1725 in Puerto Madero, Buenos Aires.
The suites were designed by Italian architect Piero Lissoni.
Each suite has floor-to-ceiling windows leading to a private balcony overlooking downtown Buenos Aires or the nearby docks.
Rooms have hardwood floors, a black and white color palette and rainfall shower heads.
The minibar is stocked with local snacks and wines.
LEYNIA is an all-day Argentinean grill influenced by flavors from Japan, built around open flame cooking.
Leynia's evening menu includes open-flame grilled meats, ossobuco empanadas, Patagonian trout ceviche and teriyaki style shrimp.
The full-service Ciel Spa has steam rooms and relaxation areas.
Spa massages and facials use the Yonka skincare brand.
The gym is open to all guests.
Rooms are listed as pet friendly.

highlights.text: The lobby has an LED-lit installation by local artist Eugenio Cuttica of fiberglass figures standing atop white chairs, in rows that extend from the lobby floor onto the wall.
The landscaping is by Enzo Enea.
The private balconies are furnished with a pair of butterfly chairs.
There is a south-facing outdoor pool with a spacious sundeck.
The hotel is a short walk from Santiago Calatrava's rotating pedestrian bridge, Puente de la Mujer, and from the Fragata Sarmiento, a historic naval ship that is now a museum.

considerations.text: Puerto Madero is a converted docklands district: its old docks and warehouses are now office buildings, apartments, restaurants and bars.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes the modern design may not suit travelers who prefer traditional luxury.
